newsitem.title: USA: World Bank president to meet Pakistan's Bhutto.
newsitem.headline: World Bank president to meet Pakistan's Bhutto.

text.p: World Bank President James Wolfensohn said he would meet Pakistan Prime Minister Benazhir Bhutto in New York on Thursday.
"I'm going up to see her for an hour, find out what is going on in her view...I'm going with no real agenda but rather as a courtesy call," he told reporters.
The World Bank has in the past criticised Pakistan for not reducing its debt fast enough and voiced concern over the size of its military spending.
Bhutto is also due to have talks with the deputy head of the International Monetary Fund, Stanley Fischer, during her current visit to New York.
The IMF withheld an $80 million tranche due in June, and part of a $600 million standby loan, pending a review of the country's 1996-97 budget.
Last year, it stopped a $1.5 billion Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility because the government had missed agreed targets.

On Wednesday, Bhutto's financial adviser, V.A. Jafarey, told the annual IMF/World Bank meeting that Pakistan was determined to restore its relationship with the two institutions and pledged to press on with economic reforms.
